data.why: A plain-lawn yard with a narrow well shaft cut into the ground, a neighbours' street of houses planted from the first frame, and a water tower built beat by beat. A tank first sits on the ground, then lifts onto legs on the word 'lift'. A crew member points from beside the well in every phase. The camera opens close on the hole being dug, follows the water from the groundwater up the pipe into the tank, out the main to the hydrant and the house fire, and ends on the finished tower.

sentences.text: If you dig a well in your yard, you have a water supply.
But the water sits far below, out of reach.
So you sink a pump and run a pipe up.
But the pump slams the pipe, and a joint bursts.
So you add a tank that catches the surge and fills.
But a ground tank only dribbles, with no push.
So you lift the tank onto legs and add a riser.
But the riser keeps pushing, and the tank spills over.
So you add an overflow pipe that carries extra water down.
But an open top and overflow pipe let dirt in.
So you add a roof, and the water stays clean.
This is a water tower.
But under that roof, the water cannot reach any house.
So you run an outlet pipe to a water main.
A tower 100 feet tall pushes water at about 43 pounds per square inch.
A tank of one million gallons weighs over 8 million pounds.
But a house fire needs more water than the main carries.
So you add a hydrant, open it, and its water sprays on the fire.
But the open hydrant drains the tank, and taps run low.
So you add a float switch that starts the pump and refills.
Add a ladder, and the well's water waits above every tap.
Congratulations, you have built a water tower.

a pump at the bottom and a pipe lift the water up
the pump pushes in violent surges and a pipe joint bursts
a tank takes the surge and fills with water
a tank on the ground has no pressure, so the water only dribbles out
lift the tank on tall legs and feed it with a riser pipe
the pump keeps pushing and the full tank spills over the rim
an overflow pipe carries the extra water safely down
the open top and the overflow pipe let dirt into the water
a roof keeps the water clean
this finished tank on legs is a water tower
the sealed tank has no way to send water to the houses
an outlet pipe leads the water down into a main
the height of the water itself makes the pressure, with no pump needed at the tap
the tank holds an enormous weight of water
a house fire needs far more water than the main carries at once
a hydrant taps the stored water and sprays it on the fire
the open hydrant drains the tank so the taps run low
a float switch starts the pump when the level falls and refills the tank
the ladder completes the tower and the well's water waits high above every tap
you have built a water tower
